reviews.comment: He is okay. His lectures are boring and not helpful, I only went for attendance. You will be fine as long as you do the homework and try to understand what you are doing. He gives out HW questions to look over for the test, as long as can do those you're fine. He is a nice professor and helpful when you ask, but his lectures are what hold him back.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I wish I could give him a higher rating, bc he's a nice guy but he is just not a good lecturer. I think after the first exam everyone realized they were better off learning from chatgpt and doing the HWs, which take a while but are very helpful for studying and learning. I stopped going to lectures and ended w a comfortable A by self-teaching

Homeworks are long and tedious until after the second exam. You will have to teach yrself. Exams and especially the final are heavily weighted. MCQs are dangerous since getting one wrong will drop the exam grade by a letter, but he will sometimes give partial credit for something like a sign error. No curve but a small bump if you've been attending
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I personally found his lectures to be okay. The homework can be long, but doable if you pay attention in lectures. His exams are a copy of the homework problems, but your grade can drop significantly because it's mostly multiple choice problems with no partial credit. Overall, he's a pretty nice teacher and not a terrible choice for MATH 311.

Not the end of the world if you have to take him HOWEVER it is if you bomb an exam. 2 midterms (20% each) and a final (40%) which are almost identical to the HW but with different numbers. MEMORIZE how to do EVERY HW problem and you'll succeed. Lectures are useless and notes are hard to read but he is helpful in office hours and overall a nice guy.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Zhou is not the greatest at teaching 311, all his lectures notes are pre-written online in bad handwriting, but he does make the exams very doable, there are basically the homework questions he gives to review for the exam. The final is 40% of your total grade which is a bit scary and it's cumulative.

His lectures suck and they are basiclly a copy of the textbook with the exact same examples and he wont work out any problems. His tests, however, are basically the homework problems, so if you learn from the textbook and do all the hw problems, you'll do well. There is a lot of hw tho so it can be hard to cover but he gives a lot of partial on tst
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This might've been the easiest class I had in my freshmen fall semester. I showed up and played Pokemon in class everyday, and I was chilling. Only assignments were homework and exams. The professor is so funny; the few moments I looked up in class made me chuckle. I spent probably 2 hours per week doing homework, so it was pretty chill.

Incomprehensible lectures, and not just because of his very strong accent. Writes notes in illegible handwriting before class and just reads off the board. Be prepared to learn the whole class on your own time. Time consuming hws that must be done on paper. Tests were mostly fair, but little review materials. Take anyone else.

Do not take this class if you want to learn. He seems like a good guy but doesn't have a real clue how to teach. He just reads through his prewritten bad handwritting notes super fast, and then expects us to understand.

You will probably learn nothing during lectures so be prepared to learn everything by yourself with his notes, all the while not being able to communicate with him since he responds so late. Also, enjoy not being able to see your grades since he uses his own website and doesn't use Canvas to upload or post anything related to his class.

The notes that Dr.Zhou posts are very low resolution and hard to read, but he goes over literally everything in lecture and explains fairly thoroughly. The textbook is helpful, especially to read before going into class to have some baseline knowledge of the material bc it is fairly difficult. Do the homework and you'll do well on the exams.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Zhou has very poor lectures, as he simply projects PDFs of pre-written notes with poor handwriting and lectures over them with a thick, hard-to-understand accent, but Zhou truly cares about his students and handles logistics/grading accordingly. Exams are based on the HW and you can bring a formula sheet, so if you do the HW, you will do just fine.

Lectures were useless in learning the material. During lectures, Zhou simply projects a pdf of digitally, poorly hand-written notes and goes through them. His "notes" are just a 1:1 copy of the textbook and its simple example problems. It's difficult to read his handwriting and understand his accent. Little to no useful examples are done in class.

Lectures were pretty decent. Very interesting course but hard to learn through lecture format. Exams were heavily weighted. Zhou really wants you to attend class and will hold it against you for missing.
reviews.ratingTags: So many papers--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Unlike nearly everyone, I tried to pay attention the whole class, but I could not help it and would battle sleep the last 80% of the class. His grading is fair though. You get cheat sheets on your exams which can carry you through an exam.

Honestly this guy can't teach. Poor communication skills(not even referring to his accent) and lack of awareness of his students just lead to a poor learning environment. All that really matters in this class is if you know how to do the homeworks or not so don't just copy off chegg.

Takes attendance. Lectures are just him going over material straight from the textbook. Hard to understand and the beginning will feel like the worst class ever but it gets better as you start to understand it. Bad at lecturing overall but tests are straight from HWs and allows a cheat sheet. Easy class if you do the HWs and understand them.

His lectures are guided by the materials he provides. The source is his handwriting and is very difficult to recognize. His lecture is simply to read the notes. His classes are not suitable for understanding so many concepts. He doesn't respect his students, he just reads his material. I will never take this professor's lectures again.
Honestly, wasn't that bad as people are saying. Yes, you have to do some self-learning, but he was always helpful if you asked him anything. If you do the homework and study, then you'll do fine.

His English is poor & hard to understand & he just shows you a pdf of his notes where he has an unreadable handwriting. So you will not learn anything from him, its just a self teach course.
His tests are straight up from the HW (tells u that on day 1) with changed numbers, you can get a good grade by memorizing how to do every single HW problem.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am not a fan of his teaching method. He pulls up his lecture notes that are PRE-WRITTEN and just reads off it the entire class. Does not work out a single problem with you. Just shows you pre-written notes from his previous semesters and straight up reads them word for word. Homework is sooo long and exams are quite tough.

This prof is so nice and respectful, and he gives lots of curves and extra points, but his way of teaching makes the course a lot harder than it should be. You pretty much have to teach yourself everything. He shows you a piece of notepaper with his handwritten notes and talks about problems instead of solving them in class.

Notes are handwritten on lined yellow paper before class and then uploaded. The notes are difficult to read and his English is even worse. Nothing is solved real-time and almost no examples are done in class. This structure might work for some classes, but math is something I struggle to grasp when I'm busy trying to understand what I'm looking at.

This guy has difficult to read notes, which comes straight from the textbook. During class, he basically recites what is on his notes and doesn't really explain anything. His accent also doesn't make it any easier. In order to actually understand the material, you will need be learning straight from the book.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Zhou's teaching methods really didn't work for me. He taught by projecting a piece of paper where he would hand write the math for the lecture - He never used power points and his "lecture sheet" would get very crowded and hard to understand. Additionally, the homework's he assigned were 50+ questions with a,b,c,d parts.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All he does is read the lecture notes he posts online; doesn't work out any problems, which I do not like in a math prof. However, tests are based on the homeworks, and he allows you to bring a formula sheet to each test, so it is doable. 3 tests, weekly homework, and optional final. Used attendance to decide whose grades to bump up.

Zhou is friendly, but his lectures are utterly unhelpful. He doesn't write anything on the board, he just points to prewritten notes. This doesn't work for math. Homework is among the most brutal I've ever seen. This is lined up to be the first college course I will score below a B in, and may even have to retake. Get someone else if you can.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This professor's accent is so thick I stopped going to lectures because I couldn't understand him. His lectures consist of him reviewing notes that he wrote beforehand. About 25% of the class doesn't show up because they don't understand him, and people that stay just work on HW from other classes (there are some ppl that listen). Don't recommend.

This is one very tough class. His accent is pretty tough to understand and the material is hard in general. This class takes a lot of work and in order to succeed make sure you do the long homework without Chegg.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I'm not a fan of his teaching style... he pretty much points to an example problem he's already solved ahead of time and explains it. This might work for other subjects, but for math I feel like problems should be solved in real time. Tests are exactly like the homework, so they shouldn't be too bad. He also bumps if you've been going to class.

I really enjoyed having this professor. His accent can be difficult to understand at times, however, more often than not, he is very clear. The homework is more difficult than the exams so try to really understand that and the course should be easy. You won't have to take the final if you like your grade before it and no MATLAB stuff.

He goes through the lecture so fast, usually ahead of other sessions 2 or 3 lectures. He gives tons of homework as well. But overall, he can explains the materials well, IF  you can CONCENTRATE and follow what he's talking about the whole time.

Great professor. He does have an accent but it isn't too difficult to understand him. He explains the material very well. The class is difficult, but he works with you to make sure you understand it. Final for the class is optional if you are happy with your grade on the first 3 exams.

Best 308 Prof! English isn't the greatest, but all his notes are posted online and very helpful. No Matlab. Homework is straight out of the book, and so is the test so learn the homework problems (chegg helps). You get formula sheet for midterms, if you are satisfied with your midterms averaged grade you can skip the final. Go to class for +1+2
